My name is Ishmael. Several years ago, I had little money and no particular reason to stay on shore, so I decided to sail and see the watery part of the world. This is how I address low spirits and improve my circulation.

You can recognize the signs when they appear: a grim set to my mouth, a damp and drizzly November feeling in my soul, or an involuntary habit of pausing in front of coffin warehouses and joining the rear of every funeral procession I pass. When my low moods become severe enough that I need real self-control to avoid stepping into the street and knocking off people's hats, I know it is time to go to sea. This practice serves as my alternative to a pistol and a bullet. Cato ends his life with a philosophical flourish and his sword; I board a ship instead.

This response is not unusual. Most people, if they examine themselves honestly, hold feelings toward the ocean similar to mine.
